column3: “Brotherly love” is rendered “love of the brethren,” and “abide” “continue.”
NASB supplies “to strangers” and “without knowing it.”
“Bound with them” is rendered “as though in prison with them.”
NASB follows the critical text (“for”); “sexually immoral” is rendered “fornicators.”
“Manner of life” is rendered “character,” and “without covetousness” “free from the love of money.”
“We are confident to say” is rendered “we confidently say.”
“Leading” is rendered “led,” and “outcome of their way of life” “result of their conduct.”
“To the ages” is rendered “forever”; NASB adds “yes and.”
NASB follows the critical text (“carried away”; “those who were thus occupied”).
“Authority” is rendered “right.”
NASB restructures the verse.
Close to the Greek.
NASB adds “Hence.”
NASB supplies “the city which is.”
“Confessing” is rendered “give thanks to.”
Close to the Greek.
“Those leading you” is rendered “your leaders”; NASB adds “Let them.”
NASB follows the critical text (“we are sure”); “well” is rendered “honorably.”
NASB adds “all.”
“Brought out” is rendered “brought up”; NASB adds “even.”
NASB follows the critical text (“every good thing,” “working in us”).
“Brothers” is rendered “brethren,” and “in few words” “briefly.”
NASB follows the critical text (“our brother”); “you know” is rendered “Take notice.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text, without the “Amen” and closing note found in the Textus Receptus.
